PELAV

Privacy Policy

Version 2.0 · Last updated 14 October 2026

PELAV ("the App") is provided by Continuum Dataguard Technologies ("we", "us", "our"). This Privacy Policy explains what personal information PELAV processes, why, who else receives it, how long it is kept, and the choices and rights you have.

1. Who is responsible

Responsible party: Continuum Dataguard Technologies. Registration number: 2026/247252/07. Physical address: Durban, KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa.

Information Officer: Pranesh Ramkhelawan, enzo@continuumdataguardtech.co.za.

Contact: admin@continuumdataguardtech.co.za.

2. Age requirement

PELAV is only for people aged 18 or older. You must confirm that you are 18 or older when you create an account, and again whenever you accept updated Terms and this Privacy Policy. We do not knowingly collect personal information from anyone under 18. If you believe someone under 18 has an account, contact us and we will delete it.

3. Information we collect and why

3.1 Account information

When you create an account we collect your email address and a password. The password is handled by our authentication provider (Supabase Auth) and stored only in hashed form; we never see it in plain text. We use your email address to run your account, to send account emails (confirming your email address and resetting your password), and to contact you about your account where necessary. You need an email address and a password to create an account; without them you cannot use the App.

Our authentication service also keeps an audit log of account events (for example sign-up, sign-in, sign-out, session refresh and account deletion). Each entry records the event, its time, your account identifier and your email address, and can record an IP address.

3.2 Legal acceptance records

When you accept the Terms and Conditions and this Privacy Policy, our server records the versions you accepted, the date and time, your confirmation that you are 18 or older, and whether you accepted at sign-up or later in the App. We keep these records to show what you agreed to. Records from before version 2.0 that were filled in automatically by an earlier version of our system are labelled as such and are not treated as your acceptance of version 2.0.

3.3 Location

With your permission, PELAV uses your device's precise location while you are using the App. PELAV does not track your location in the background. You can refuse or withdraw location permission in your device settings; Home and Marine still work with reduced features.

Your location is used as follows:

  • Current conditions (Home and Marine screens). Your device first converts its position into a grid area of about 5 km (0.05 degrees) and sends only the centre of that grid area, not your exact position, to PELAV's backend. The backend requests current weather and sea conditions for that grid area from Open-Meteo under PELAV's paid Open-Meteo subscription. Open-Meteo receives the grid-area centre from our backend, not your exact position and not your account details. The results are cached on our backend against the grid area, not against you or your account. Because the conditions are for the grid area, they can differ from conditions at your exact spot.
  • Tides. Your device sends its coordinates to PELAV's backend, which rounds them to about 1.1 km (two decimal places) before requesting tide predictions from WorldTides. WorldTides never receives your exact location or your account details. Our backend does not store your exact coordinates; the tide cache holds only the rounded coordinates (section 7).
  • Maps. Map images come from OpenStreetMap. Your device requests map tiles directly from OpenStreetMap's servers for the area on screen. When the map is centred on you, this reveals your approximate location (depending on zoom) and your IP address to OpenStreetMap, as with any web request. OpenStreetMap does not receive your PELAV account details.

Your device's coordinates are not stored in your account, your catch history or your fishing sessions. When you are signed in, our backend knows which account asks for conditions at the time of the request (to apply the refresh limits in 3.6), but it does not record the location or grid area against your account.

3.4 Catches and fishing sessions

When you log a catch, we store what you enter: species, location, weight, length, bait, hook, trace, notes, and date and time. The location of a catch is a place name you choose from PELAV's fishing-spot directory or type yourself, not GPS coordinates. Your catch record has a photo field, but this version of the App does not let you attach photos.

When you start a fishing session we store a session identifier, start time, location label (a place name, or the words "Current Location"), target species, and, where available, a snapshot of weather, sea and tide conditions taken at the start of the session. When the session ends we store the end time and status (active, ended or abandoned). A session does not track your location while it is open. If about 12 hours pass we may ask whether you are still fishing; if about 72 hours pass without you returning, the session is marked abandoned. An abandoned session is not presented as a no-catch result.

This information is linked to your account so that you can see your history. Database rules allow only your account to read or change it through the App.

3.5 Access records

This version of the App is free. It has no Premium tier, does not sell subscriptions and does not offer free trials; every feature is available to every account. When it starts, the App still asks our server for your account's access status. Our server's access records can hold a free trial (start and end time), a paid subscription (a hashed reference to the purchase, the product, its state and expiry), complimentary access (its reason, who granted it, and when it starts and ends) and, for accounts created with earlier versions of the App, whether the account had Premium in those versions. This version of the App does not create trial or subscription records. These records are linked to your account and are deleted with it.

3.6 Refresh limits

To keep the service available for everyone, our server counts how often your account asks for fresh conditions within a short time window. Each count covers one hour. How long counts are kept is set out in section 7.

3.7 Crash reports

PELAV uses Firebase Crashlytics (Google) to find and fix crashes. When the App crashes, Crashlytics receives a crash report containing technical information such as the stack trace, device model, operating-system version and app version, together with Crashlytics and Firebase installation identifiers. PELAV does not attach your email address or account identifier to crash reports. How long Google keeps crash reports is set out in section 7.

3.8 Information kept only on your device

Some information never leaves your device:

  • Digital Fishing Licence Vault. The Vault is not available in this version of the App. If you stored a licence document with an earlier version, the licence PDF and the details you typed in (angler name, licence number, issuing authority, dates and the original file name) remain only in the App's private storage on your device, separately for each PELAV account signed in on that device. PELAV does not upload them and has no access to them. You can remove them by deleting your account in the App (section 8), by clearing the App's data in your device settings, or uninstalling the App.
  • Your sign-in session, your appearance setting, and a note that your account has accepted the current legal documents (so the App can open when you are offline).
  • The most recent current-conditions results for up to five grid areas, so the App can show them, marked with their age, when you are offline. They are stored by grid area, never with your exact position.

PELAV tells Android not to include any of this in device backups or device-to-device transfers. If you lose or reset your device, any Licence Vault document stored on it is gone. Your account data is held on our servers and returns when you sign in.

3.9 Recommending PELAV

If you use Recommend a Friend, your device's own share sheet sends a short text that you choose where to send. PELAV does not see who you share it with.

3.10 Older versions of the App

Section 3.3 describes the current version of the App. Versions 1.3.0 and older work differently for current conditions on the Home and Marine screens: if you still use one of those versions, your device sends its coordinates directly to Open-Meteo's free service, without passing through PELAV's backend. Open-Meteo does not receive your PELAV account details. Updating to the current version ends this. Tides and maps work as described in 3.3 in those versions too.

4. Lawful basis for processing

We process personal information only where section 11(1) of the Protection of Personal Information Act 4 of 2013 (POPIA) allows it, and only as much as each purpose needs:

To provide the App you signed up for (section 11(1)(b), performance of our agreement with you, which is our Terms and Conditions):

  • your account, sign-in and account emails (3.1);
  • your catch and session records (3.4);
  • your access records (3.5);
  • your device's location, used to show nearby fishing spots and to fetch conditions and tides for your area (3.3);
  • deleting your account (section 8).

You choose whether PELAV may use your location through your device's location permission, and you can turn it off at any time; some features are then limited.

Our legitimate interests (section 11(1)(f)):

  • keeping a record of the legal documents you accepted, so that we can show what you agreed to (3.2);
  • protecting accounts and the service against misuse, through the authentication audit log (3.1) and refresh limits (3.6);
  • finding and fixing crashes, through crash reports that carry no email address or account identifier (3.7).

Each record is limited to what that purpose needs and is kept only for the period in section 7. You can object to this processing on reasonable grounds relating to your particular situation (section 9).

Obligations imposed by law (section 11(1)(c)):

  • keeping encrypted backups as one of the security safeguards that section 19 of POPIA requires;
  • notifying security compromises (section 10);
  • responding to the Information Regulator or to other lawful requests.

We do not rely on your consent for any of this processing, and we do not use your personal information for direct marketing.

5. Who receives your information

We use these service providers. Each processes information only as needed to provide its service to PELAV, under its own terms and privacy practices.

  • Supabase (authentication, database, backend functions): account, legal-acceptance, catch, session, access and refresh-limit records. Our Supabase project is hosted in the European Union (Ireland).
  • Resend (sending account emails on behalf of our authentication service): your email address and the content of account emails.
  • Google Firebase Crashlytics: crash reports as described in 3.7.
  • Open-Meteo: the centre of a grid area of about 5 km, sent by our backend, for current conditions (3.3). For older App versions, see 3.10. Open-Meteo states that it keeps web-server logs containing IP addresses and coordinates for 90 days.
  • WorldTides (Brainware LLC): rounded coordinates (about 1.1 km), sent by our backend.
  • OpenStreetMap: map-tile requests from your device, as described in 3.3.

We do not sell your personal information, and we do not share it for advertising.

6. Information processed outside South Africa

All of these providers are outside South Africa:

  • Supabase: our project is hosted in Ireland (European Union). Supabase's data processing addendum forms part of its terms of service.
  • Resend: processes mainly in the United States. Resend's data processing addendum forms part of its terms of service.
  • Google Firebase Crashlytics: Google may process crash reports in any country where it or its agents have facilities.
  • Open-Meteo: operated from Switzerland.
  • WorldTides: operated by Brainware LLC in California, United States.
  • OpenStreetMap: the OpenStreetMap Foundation stores tile-request data in the United Kingdom and the Netherlands, and map tiles are delivered through a content delivery network.

The level of protection differs by country:

  • the European Union applies the General Data Protection Regulation;
  • the United Kingdom applies the UK GDPR;
  • Switzerland applies its Federal Act on Data Protection;
  • the United States has no general federal data-protection law comparable to POPIA.

We transfer personal information to these providers because the transfer is necessary to perform our agreement with you, that is to provide, maintain and fix the App you use (section 72(1)(c) of POPIA). Each provider receives only the information listed in section 5.

7. How long we keep information

  • Account, catches, sessions, legal-acceptance records, access records: until you delete your account (section 8).
  • Refresh counters: no more than two days. Each counter covers one hour, and counters are deleted daily once their hour is over a day old, or with your account.
  • Authentication audit log (3.1): entries are not removed when you delete your account. They are kept for up to 90 days.
  • Tide cache: used for up to about 12 hours (or until the next midnight, South African time), then deleted by a daily job 7 to 8 days after it expires. It holds rounded coordinates and tide data, not your account.
  • Current-conditions cache and provider-call records: hold a grid area of about 5 km, the time and the provider's data, not your account. A cache entry is replaced each time its grid area is refreshed, and deleted no later than 30 days after its grid area was last refreshed. Provider-call records are kept for up to 90 days.
  • Crash reports: Google states that it keeps crash stack traces and their identifiers for 90 days before starting to remove them from its live and backup systems.
  • Disaster-recovery backups: we keep encrypted, offline backups of our database to recover from serious failures. Information in a backup may remain until that backup is replaced or destroyed. Each backup is kept for up to 90 days. Our database provider, Supabase, may also keep automatic backups of our database under its own terms, for the period its plan sets (Supabase publishes periods of up to 30 days).
  • On your device: until you delete it in the App where the App offers that, delete your account, clear the App's data in your device settings, or uninstall the App. A Licence Vault document stored with an earlier version of the App can only be removed in one of the last three ways.

8. Deleting your account

You can delete your account at any time in the App: Profile > Delete Account. You can also do this from the screen that asks you to accept updated terms, without accepting them. Deletion:

  • permanently deletes, on our servers, your account, profile, catches, fishing sessions, legal-acceptance records, refresh counters, and the access records described in 3.5 (any trial, subscription or complimentary-access records). Catches and sessions are deleted together in a single database transaction, so a failure never leaves only part of them deleted;
  • then removes, on that device, the Licence Vault document stored for your account, and signs you out.

Information that deletion does not remove is listed in section 7: authentication audit-log entries, crash reports already sent, provider logs, and disaster-recovery backups until they are replaced.

The on-device cleanup happens after the server deletion succeeds and depends on the App being able to run it; if it does not complete, uninstalling the App removes it.

If you cannot use the App, email admin@continuumdataguardtech.co.za from the email address of your PELAV account and ask us to delete it. We will verify the request and process it as soon as reasonably possible. Full details are on our account deletion page.

9. Your rights

Under POPIA you have the right:

  • to ask, free of charge, whether we hold personal information about you, and to request access to it (section 23);
  • to ask us to correct, destroy or delete it (section 24);
  • to object, on reasonable grounds relating to your particular situation, to processing based on our legitimate interests (section 11(3)(a));
  • to be told if your personal information has been accessed or acquired by an unauthorised person (section 22).

If you object, we stop that processing unless the law provides for it. If we can no longer protect or run your account without it, you can delete the account. You can turn off location permission at any time in your device settings.

To exercise these rights, contact us at admin@continuumdataguardtech.co.za. We may ask you to confirm your identity first, normally by writing from your account's email address.

You also have the right to complain to the Information Regulator of South Africa:

  • Woodmead North Office Park, 54 Maxwell Drive, Woodmead, Johannesburg, 2191
  • POPIAComplaints@inforegulator.org.za
  • inforegulator.org.za

10. Security

We use encrypted connections, access controls in our database that keep each account's records separate, and server-side handling of provider credentials. Our own backups are encrypted. No system is completely secure, and we cannot guarantee absolute security. If there are reasonable grounds to believe that your personal information has been accessed or acquired by an unauthorised person, we will notify the Information Regulator and you, as section 22 of POPIA requires. We will do so as soon as reasonably possible after we discover the compromise, taking into account the legitimate needs of law enforcement and the steps needed to determine its scope and restore the integrity of our systems. We will delay telling you only if a public body responsible for investigating offences, or the Information Regulator, decides that notifying you would impede a criminal investigation. We will tell you in writing, normally by email to your account's email address, with enough information for you to protect yourself: the possible consequences, what we have done or will do about it, what we recommend you do and, if known, who accessed or acquired the information. We cannot notify you if we cannot establish your identity.

11. Changes to this policy

When we change this policy we publish a new version with a new version number and date. When the Terms or this Privacy Policy change, the App asks you to read and accept the new versions before you continue; you can instead sign out or delete your account. We do not treat continued use as acceptance.
